w: Everyone here still calls it Azure Villas, the name it wore before the National Register got involved. Tucked into Miami Springs at 200 Azure Way, it made the historic-places list in 1985, a quiet holdover from the city's boom-era hotel building spree.
s: The apartment hotel that still goes by its old alias
_facts: also known as Azure Villas
located at 200 Azure Way, Miami Springs
added to NRHP November 1, 1985

w: A Pueblo Revival oddity in Spanish-tiled Miami Springs, its U-shaped walls have sheltered two very different careers - Ray Millard, Hialeah's first postmaster, then from 1947 mayor William McCarty. Finished around 1926, it made the National Register in 1986.
s: A postmaster's house, then a mayor's
_facts: two-story Pueblo Revival U-shaped house completed around 1926
first owner Ray Millard, first postmaster of Hialeah
owned 1947-1985 by William McCarty, mayor of Miami Beach 1948-51
added to NRHP in 1986

w: James Deering built his International Harvester fortune into a Venetian fantasy on Biscayne Bay, a Mediterranean Revival villa wrapped in Italian Renaissance gardens and a whole outbuildings village. Miami-Dade County now runs it as a museum, gardens and all, one Metrorail stop from downtown.
s: A harvester fortune poured into a Venetian villa
_facts: former villa and estate of James Deering of the Deering McCormick-International Harvester fortune
Italian Renaissance gardens and historic village outbuildings compound
Mediterranean Revival architecture with Baroque elements
now owned by Miami-Dade County and open to the public, served by Vizcaya Metrorail station

w: Founded in 1984 as the Center for the Fine Arts, it spent decades quietly building a collection before Herzog & de Meuron gave it a showcase worthy of it, a Biscayne Bay building it moved into in 2013. Over 150,000 people showed up in the first four months alone.
s: The fine-arts center that outgrew its old name
_facts: founded 1984 as Center for the Fine Arts, renamed Miami Art Museum in 1996, then PAMM in 2013
relocated 2013 to Maurice A. Ferre Park in a building designed by Herzog & de Meuron
over 150,000 visitors in its first four months at the new building

w: Nineteen thousand objects spanning five thousand years of human creativity, sorted into fourteen themed rooms on a university campus in Coral Gables. The Palley Pavilion alone is worth the detour, a glass collection paired with an outdoor sculpture garden.
s: Five thousand years of art in fourteen rooms
_facts: collection of more than 19,250 objects representing more than 5,000 years of human creativity
14 thematic rooms plus the Palley Pavilion for the glass collection
art museum of the University of Miami in Coral Gables, accessible by Metrorail's University Station

w: Thirty acres of downtown waterfront built in 1976 on the old Seaboard Air Line Railroad slips, first named Bicentennial Park for America's 200th birthday. Wedged between Biscayne Bay and the arena crowds, it's since been rebuilt into Miami's museum-district green space.
s: Bicentennial Park's second act as museum green
_facts: 30-acre public urban park opened in 1976 on the site of former Seaboard Air Line Railroad slips
originally named Bicentennial Park for the US bicentennial
bordered by Biscayne Bay, Biscayne Boulevard and the arena, maintained by the Bayfront Park Management Trust

w: Finished in 1928 after four years of construction, it briefly out-topped every building south of the Mason-Dixon line at 361 feet and 28 floors. It's still Miami-Dade's working civil courthouse today, a Jazz Age skyscraper that never stopped clocking in.
s: The skyscraper that briefly ruled the whole South
_facts: constructed 1925-28 at 73 West Flagler Street
361 feet tall with 28 floors, tallest building in Miami, Florida and south of the Mason-Dixon line when built
added to NRHP January 4, 1989; still in use as the main civil courthouse

w: A racetrack so grand it earned National Register status back in 1979, a 1-1/8 mile main oval wrapped around an inner turf course, sprawled across forty city blocks of Hialeah. Decades on, the grandstand still outlasts most of what ever raced across it.
s: Forty city blocks built for one racetrack
_facts: main track 1-1/8 miles long with an inner turf course
site covers 40 square blocks of central-east Hialeah
added to the NRHP in 1979

w: Built in 1896, it's the oldest Catholic church in Miami still standing on Northeast 2nd Street, a downtown survivor that made the National Register in 1974, decades before the skyscrapers grew up around it.
s: Miami's oldest Catholic church, still standing
_facts: built in 1896, the oldest Catholic church in Miami
located at 118 Northeast 2nd Street
added to NRHP on July 18, 1974
